title: What If a Wave Taller Than a Skyscraper Hit Alaska? One Did

scenes.text: What if a wave rose taller than the Empire State Building? In 1958, one did.
At night, an earthquake shook a narrow Alaskan bay, and about 30 million cubic meters of rock slid into the water.
The splash climbed the mountainside to 524 meters, the highest wave run-up ever recorded.
It stripped the forest off the slopes and swept through the bay at roughly 180 kilometers an hour.
Three fishing boats were anchored inside. Two were lost, and only one stayed afloat.
This was not a normal tsunami from the sea floor. A landslide made it, which is why it climbed so high.

description:
What if a wave rose taller than the Empire State Building?
In 1958 a landslide in an Alaskan bay sent water 524 meters up a mountainside, the highest wave run-up ever recorded.
